lessons.title: Understanding Duck Social Structure
lessons.body: Ducks are flock animals with a clear pecking order. In a typical backyard flock of 10 to 20 ducks, you will see one or two dominant males and several females. The dominant male leads the group to food and water and warns of danger. If you keep too many males, fighting increases and females get injured. A good ratio is 1 male to 4 or 5 females. For example, if you have 12 females, keep only 2 or 3 males. Observe your flock daily: the ducks that eat first and walk in front are the leaders. Handle the leaders gently so they remain calm; stressed leaders make the whole flock nervous. Ducks recognize each other by voice and facial features. When you introduce new ducks, do it slowly. Put the new ducks in a separate pen next to the flock for 3 to 5 days so they can see and hear each other. Then mix them at night when it is dark. This reduces fighting. In Africa, many farmers keep ducks in free-range systems during the day and house them at night. Provide enough space: at least 1 square meter per duck inside the house and 3 to 4 square meters per duck in the outdoor run. If space is tight, aggression rises. Also, ducks bond strongly with their group. If you remove one duck for more than a few days, reintroduce it carefully. Always provide multiple feeding and watering stations so lower-ranking ducks can eat without being bullied. With patience, you can maintain a peaceful flock.

lessons.title: Low-Stress Handling Techniques
lessons.body: Ducks stress easily. A stressed duck may stop laying eggs for days or get sick. To handle ducks calmly, never chase them. Move slowly and speak softly. Use a herding stick or a piece of cloth tied to a stick to guide them, not to hit. For catching a duck, use a corner of the pen. Walk behind the duck and gently guide it into a corner. Then place both hands over the wings, holding the wings against the body. Lift the duck with one hand under the breast and the other supporting the belly. Never lift a duck by its neck, wings, or legs. Hold it close to your body so it feels secure. If you need to examine a duck, tuck its head under your arm gently to keep it calm. For moving a group, use a portable fence made of bamboo or plastic mesh. Set up a funnel shape to guide ducks into a new area. Ducks follow each other, so if you lead one, the rest will follow. Use feed as a reward: shake a container of maize or pellets and they will come. In Africa, many farmers use a simple call like 'kwa kwa kwa' when feeding. Train your ducks to associate that call with food. Then you can move them anywhere without stress. Always handle ducks in the cool of the morning or evening, not during the heat of the day. Keep handling sessions short, under 10 minutes. If a duck pants or flaps wildly, put it down and let it rest. With gentle, consistent handling, ducks become tame and easy to manage.

lessons.title: Moving and Transporting Ducks
lessons.body: Moving ducks from one place to another requires planning. For short distances, up to 500 meters, you can herd them slowly. Use two people: one behind and one on the side. Walk at the speed of the slowest duck. For longer distances, use a pickup truck or a bicycle trailer. Never transport ducks in a closed boot or sack. They need air. Use crates with holes on all sides. A crate of 60 cm by 90 cm can hold 6 to 8 adult ducks comfortably. Put a layer of dry grass or wood shavings on the floor to absorb droppings. Transport in the early morning or late evening when it is cool. If the journey is more than 2 hours, stop every hour to check on them. Give water but not feed, as feed can cause vomiting. In hot African conditions, sprinkle water on the ducks' feet to cool them. Avoid overcrowding: if ducks are piled on top of each other, they can suffocate. For air travel or long-distance trucking, use specially designed poultry crates and consult a veterinarian for health certificates. When you arrive, let the ducks rest in a shaded, quiet place for at least 2 hours before releasing them into the new pen. Provide water with electrolytes or a little sugar to help them recover. If you are moving ducks to a new home, keep them locked inside the new house for 3 to 5 days so they learn it is home. Then open the door to the outside run. This prevents them from running away. Always check local regulations for moving livestock across districts.

lessons.title: Training Ducks for Routine Management
lessons.body: Ducks are smart and can learn routines quickly. Training makes daily tasks easier and reduces stress for both you and the birds. Start with a feeding call. Every time you feed, make the same sound, such as a whistle or 'duck duck duck'. After 5 to 7 days, the ducks will come running when they hear it. Use this call to move them from the run to the house in the evening. For example, at 6 pm, call and sprinkle a little grain near the house door. Soon they will go inside on their own. Next, train them to use a ramp or steps to enter a raised house. Place a plank at a gentle slope, 30 to 40 degrees. Put feed along the ramp. Ducks will follow the feed. After a few days, they will use the ramp without feed. To train ducks to stay in a specific area, use a low fence of 60 cm height. Ducks rarely fly over low fences if they have food and water inside. For health checks, train them to stand on a weighing scale. Put the scale near the feeding area. Place a little feed on the scale. Let them eat from it. Gradually, you can weigh them weekly. This helps you monitor growth. For egg collection, train ducks to lay in nest boxes. Put a fake egg or a golf ball in each nest box. Keep the boxes dark and private. Most ducks will start using them within a week. Always reward with feed or praise. Never punish. Ducks remember bad experiences and become difficult to handle. With consistent training, your flock will be easy to manage, saving you time and labour.

lessons.title: Preventing Feather Pecking and Aggression
lessons.body: Feather pecking is when ducks pull each other's feathers. It can lead to bleeding, infection, and even death. The main causes are overcrowding, boredom, lack of feed, or too much light. To prevent it, first check your space. You need at least 1 square meter per duck inside and 3 to 4 square meters outside. If you have 20 ducks, the house should be at least 20 square meters. Second, provide enough feeders and drinkers. A good rule is one feeder for every 6 ducks and one drinker for every 8 ducks. Spread them out so bullies cannot guard all the food. Third, give them things to do. Ducks love to forage. Throw a handful of maize or greens into the straw or mud. They will spend hours digging. You can also hang a cabbage or lettuce head from a string. They will peck at it instead of each other. Fourth, check the diet. A lack of protein or salt can cause pecking. Provide a balanced feed with 16 to 18 percent protein for layers. Add a mineral block or oyster shells. Fifth, reduce bright light. Ducks need 14 hours of light for laying, but too much bright light increases aggression. Use dim red or blue light if possible. If you see a duck being pecked, remove it immediately. Put it in a separate pen for a few days. Treat wounds with an antiseptic like iodine. Do not use Vaseline or oil, as it attracts more pecking. If aggression is severe, isolate the bully for 3 to 5 days. When you return it, the pecking order may reset. In Africa, many farmers use wood ash in the dust bath to reduce skin irritation. Always act early.

lessons.title: Enrichment for Mental and Physical Health
lessons.body: Ducks are curious and need stimulation. Without enrichment, they get bored, stressed, and may develop bad habits like feather pecking or egg eating. Enrichment means giving them things to explore, play with, and forage. One simple method is a dust bath. Ducks love to bathe in dry soil or sand. Dig a shallow pit, 1 meter by 1 meter, and fill it with a mix of sand, wood ash, and dry soil. This helps them clean their feathers and reduces parasites. Another is a small pool. Ducks need water to swim and mate. A child's wading pool or a half-cut drum works well. Change the water daily to prevent disease. If you cannot provide a pool, give them a trough deep enough to dip their heads. Foraging is the best enrichment. Scatter feed in a pile of leaves or straw. Ducks will spend hours turning it over. You can also hang a bunch of greens like kale or spinach from a string at duck height. They will jump and peck at it. Rotate toys to keep interest. A simple ball or a plastic bottle with holes and filled with grain can be a puzzle feeder. Ducks will roll it to get the grain. Provide perches: a low log or a plank 15 cm off the ground. Ducks like to rest on them. Also, play soft music or radio during the day. This reduces stress from sudden noises. In Africa, many farmers use old tyres cut in half as pools or feeders. Be creative with local materials. Change the enrichment weekly. Observe your ducks: if they are active, curious, and clean, they are happy. If they sit in corners or peck at each other, add more enrichment. A happy duck lays more eggs and tastes better.

quiz.q: What is the ideal male-to-female ratio in a duck flock to reduce fighting?
quiz.explanation: A ratio of 1 male to 4-5 females reduces competition and injury to females.

quiz.q: How long should you keep new ducks in a separate pen next to the flock before mixing them?
quiz.explanation: 3-5 days allows them to see and hear each other, reducing fighting when mixed.

quiz.q: When lifting a duck, where should you place your hands?
options: C) Over the wings and under the breast
quiz.explanation: Supporting the wings and breast prevents injury and keeps the duck calm.

quiz.q: What is a low-stress way to move a group of ducks?
options: A) Chase them with a dog
B) Use a herding stick and walk slowly
quiz.explanation: Slow movement with a guiding stick mimics natural herding and reduces panic.

quiz.q: How many adult ducks can fit in a crate of 60 cm by 90 cm for transport?
quiz.explanation: 6-8 ducks allow enough space for air and movement without overcrowding.

quiz.q: During transport, what should you give ducks if the journey is over 2 hours?
quiz.explanation: Water prevents dehydration; feed can cause vomiting and stress.

quiz.q: After transporting ducks to a new home, how long should you keep them locked inside?
quiz.explanation: Locking them in for 3-5 days helps them learn the new house as home.

quiz.q: What is the first step in training ducks to come when called?
options: A) Use a whistle only once
B) Make the same sound every time you feed
quiz.explanation: Consistent association between a sound and food trains ducks to respond.

quiz.q: How can you train ducks to use a ramp to enter a raised house?
options: B) Place feed along the ramp
quiz.explanation: Ducks follow feed, so placing it on the ramp encourages them to walk up.

quiz.q: What can you put in nest boxes to encourage ducks to lay there?
options: B) A fake egg or golf ball
quiz.explanation: A fake egg signals a safe laying spot, and ducks will add their own eggs.

quiz.q: What is a common cause of feather pecking in ducks?
quiz.explanation: Overcrowding increases stress and competition, leading to pecking.

quiz.q: How many feeders should you provide for a flock of 18 ducks?
quiz.explanation: One feeder per 6 ducks means 3 feeders for 18 ducks, reducing bullying.

quiz.q: What should you do immediately if you see a duck being pecked and bleeding?
options: B) Remove it to a separate pen
C) Put oil on the wound
quiz.explanation: Isolating the injured duck prevents further pecking and allows healing.

quiz.q: Which of these is a good enrichment activity for ducks?
options: A) Keeping them in a dark box
quiz.explanation: Hanging greens encourages natural pecking and foraging behavior.

quiz.q: Why is a dust bath important for ducks?
options: A) It helps clean feathers and reduce parasites
B) It is for drinking water
C) It is a nesting site
D) It is for storing feed
quiz.explanation: Dust bathing maintains feather health and controls external parasites.

quiz.q: How often should you change the water in a duck pool?
quiz.explanation: Daily change prevents buildup of droppings and disease.

quiz.q: What percentage of protein should layer duck feed contain?
quiz.explanation: 16-18% protein supports egg production and prevents deficiencies that cause pecking.

quiz.q: What is a good way to reduce aggression in ducks during handling?
options: A) Handle them quickly and loudly
B) Handle in the cool of the day
D) Use a stick to hit them
quiz.explanation: Cool times reduce heat stress and keep ducks calmer.

quiz.q: How long should a handling session last for a duck?
quiz.explanation: Short sessions prevent stress and overheating.

quiz.q: What should you do before introducing new ducks to an existing flock?
quiz.explanation: Quarantine allows observation for disease and reduces fighting.

quiz.q: What is a sign of a happy, well-enriched duck flock?
options: B) Active, curious, and clean ducks
quiz.explanation: Active and curious behavior indicates good mental and physical health.

quiz.q: Which local material can be used as a duck pool?
quiz.explanation: A half-cut drum holds water and is durable for swimming.

quiz.q: What should you do if a duck pants or flaps wildly during handling?
options: B) Put it down and let it rest
quiz.explanation: Signs of stress mean the duck needs a break to avoid injury or shock.

quiz.q: How can you use a call to move ducks from the run to the house?
options: A) Call and sprinkle grain near the house
C) Call and lock them out
quiz.explanation: Associating the call with a reward encourages ducks to move willingly.

quiz.q: What is a good height for a fence to keep ducks in an area?
quiz.explanation: Ducks rarely fly over a 60 cm fence if food and water are inside.

quiz.q: What can you add to a dust bath to help reduce skin irritation?
quiz.explanation: Wood ash is a natural insect repellent and soothes skin.

quiz.q: How often should you rotate enrichment toys for ducks?
quiz.explanation: Weekly rotation keeps ducks interested and prevents boredom.

quiz.q: What is a puzzle feeder for ducks?
options: B) A plastic bottle with holes and grain
quiz.explanation: The duck rolls the bottle to release grain, providing mental stimulation.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid using Vaseline on a duck's wound?
quiz.explanation: Oily substances draw attention and can lead to more pecking.

quiz.q: What is a benefit of playing soft music for ducks?
options: B) Reduces stress from sudden noises
C) Makes them lay more eggs
quiz.explanation: Soft music masks sudden sounds and calms the flock.
